events.title: Adrian IV, the only English pope, dies at Anagni
events.description: Nicholas Breakspear, Pope Adrian IV, died after a stormy pontificate dominated by conflict with Frederick Barbarossa. His death led to a disputed election and an 18-year schism.
events.html: Nicholas Breakspear, Pope Adrian IV, died after a stormy pontificate dominated by conflict with Frederick Barbarossa. His death led to a disputed election and an 18-year schism.

events.title: Louis XIV dies after 72 years on the throne
events.description: The Sun King died at Versailles days before his 77th birthday, having reigned for 72 years, the longest of any major European monarch. His five-year-old great-grandson succeeded as Louis XV.
events.html: The Sun King died at Versailles days before his 77th birthday, having reigned for 72 years, the longest of any major European monarch. His five-year-old great-grandson succeeded as Louis XV.

events.title: Aaron Burr is acquitted of treason
events.description: A jury in Richmond acquitted former Vice President Aaron Burr of plotting to wage war in the West. Chief Justice John Marshall's strict reading of treason doomed Jefferson's prosecution.
events.html: A jury in Richmond acquitted former Vice President Aaron Burr of plotting to wage war in the West. Chief Justice John Marshall's strict reading of treason doomed Jefferson's prosecution.

events.title: Confederates evacuate Atlanta
events.description: General John Bell Hood abandoned Atlanta, blowing up ammunition trains as he left, and Sherman's troops entered the next day. The capture of the rail hub revived Lincoln's re-election hopes.
events.html: General John Bell Hood abandoned Atlanta, blowing up ammunition trains as he left, and Sherman's troops entered the next day. The capture of the rail hub revived Lincoln's re-election hopes.

events.title: The Great Kantō earthquake devastates Tokyo and Yokohama
events.description: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake and the fires that followed destroyed much of Tokyo and Yokohama, killing more than 100,000 people. In the chaos, vigilantes murdered thousands of Koreans.
events.html: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake and the fires that followed destroyed much of Tokyo and Yokohama, killing more than 100,000 people. In the chaos, vigilantes murdered thousands of Koreans.

events.title: Germany invades Poland
events.description: German forces crossed into Poland at dawn without a declaration of war. Britain and France declared war two days later, and the Second World War had begun.
events.html: German forces crossed into Poland at dawn without a declaration of war. Britain and France declared war two days later, and the Second World War had begun.

events.title: Muammar Gaddafi seizes power in Libya
events.description: Junior army officers led by 27-year-old Muammar Gaddafi overthrew King Idris in a bloodless coup. Gaddafi ruled Libya for 42 years until his overthrow and death in 2011.
events.html: Junior army officers led by 27-year-old Muammar Gaddafi overthrew King Idris in a bloodless coup. Gaddafi ruled Libya for 42 years until his overthrow and death in 2011.
